summary: A fragment of a first-person thriller in which narrator Cas Russell, a brown, female, freelance fixer, is interrogated by a Fed named Jones about the Professor Halliday case. Jones doubts that 'Cas Russell' is her real name and warns she is close to being treated as a perpetrator rather than a witness. Cas insists the name is real, sarcastically offers 'Bridget Twitwaffle', and relaxes slightly on learning the Feds care about her only in connection to Halliday.
one_line: In a thriller excerpt, Cas Russell is questioned by Fed agent Jones, who disbelieves her name and demands an account of rescuing Professor Halliday.
key_facts: Cas Russell is the first-person narrator and is a foot shorter than a six-foot-tall man, brown, and female.
Jones, a Fed, leans against the wall across from Cas and says 'Cas Russell' to show she already knows her identity.
Cas reasons that Jones could have identified her by making calls to certain disreputable people, even ones she had never met.
Jones asks 'Now what's your real name?', which Cas did not expect.
Jones says the Feds don't care about Cas's spare-time activities but she is 'a fingernail's width' from going from 'witness' to 'perpetrator'.
Cas thinks that if the Feds care about her only in relation to Halliday, that could be a very good thing.
Cas insists 'Cas Russell' is her real name and says she can fool a polygraph's physiological readings but is telling the truth here.
Cas argues that burning an alias on every job would prevent her from building up a client base.
Jones suggests 'Cas Russell' is only her business name.
Cas sarcastically gives her name as 'Bridget Twitwaffle'.
Cas says she tracked down Professor Halliday and rescued her.
Jones demands a detailed account of what happened inside.
